stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating focus on large language model performance.
Key technologies involved include transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features new support via Ollama's MLX engine for DFlash and image input.

stories.title: OpenAI says its Jalapeño chip can power faster AI responses than the competition
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced a new custom AI chip named 'Jalapeño'.
The chip is claimed to offer superior performance, boasting lower latency and higher throughput compared to competitors.
This development signals a continued trend of major AI players developing proprietary hardware to optimize AI processing.

stories.title: SpaceX intends to invest up to $100 billion in massive Louisiana spaceport
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: SpaceX plans a massive investment of up to $100 billion for a new spaceport in Louisiana.
The project is described as being of unprecedented scale and significance.
This indicates a major expansion and strategic commitment by SpaceX to large-scale space infrastructure.

stories.title: New bootloader lets you take the "Meta" out of the original Meta Quest
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A new bootloader exploit has been discovered for the original Meta Quest.
The vulnerability allows for privilege escalation, granting 'full control' over the device.
This exploit effectively bypasses Meta's servers and proprietary applications.

stories.title: AI is hitting entry-level jobs hardest, Stanford study finds
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A Stanford study indicates that AI is disproportionately affecting entry-level employment.
Young workers in fields heavily impacted by AI have seen a 19% decline in employment.
The study contrasts these figures with occupations deemed more resistant to AI automation.

stories.title: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra
stories.author: interpol_p
bullet_points: Apple has announced the introduction of new high-performance chips, specifically the M6 and M5 Ultra.
The M5 Ultra is highlighted as Apple's most powerful chip to date, suggesting significant performance leaps.
The news is supported by coverage from major tech outlets like TechCrunch and 9to5Mac, indicating high industry relevance.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Jalapeño Inference Chip Could Reshape the Economics of Serving AI
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI has unveiled 'Jalapeño,' its proprietary Intelligence Processor.
Jalapeño is designed as a purpose-built chip specifically for AI inference tasks.
The introduction suggests a potential shift in the economic model for serving large-scale AI models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as an LLM.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, suggesting modern implementation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline within the transformers ecosystem.
The model is associated with Meta (formerly Facebook) and utilizes standard ML formats like safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for continuous operation, context gathering, and multi-step task execution on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
The optimization results in up to 90% faster performance, particularly when utilized with coding agents (Aider benchmark).

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: Lab supply companies have been selling antibodies using manipulated images
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Lab supply companies are reportedly selling antibodies that utilize manipulated images.
The extent of image manipulation is described as widespread among suppliers.
The quality of the manipulated images is severe enough that they would warrant retraction in scientific publications.

stories.title: AI won’t replace radiologists, but it will dramatically change their jobs
stories.author: Lola Butcher, Knowable Magazine
bullet_points: AI is set to transform the role of radiologists rather than fully replace them.
The article addresses a historical prediction that AI would completely automate radiological duties.
The shift indicates AI will become a powerful augmentation tool in medical diagnostics.

stories.title: Apple's new desktop computers are designed specifically for local AI development
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple is designing new desktop computers with a focus on local AI development capabilities.
The hardware refresh is specifically intended to support advanced AI workloads on user machines.
The design implicitly addresses the community trend of users daisy-chaining Macs for intensive AI tasks.

stories.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
stories.author: Yingcong Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'ReWorld,' an interactive world model designed to handle long-horizon memory in real-time simulations.
Addresses the structural tension between short-horizon control requirements and the need for unbounded memory.
Achieves this balance using mixed per-head attention windows, combining local context with global history attention.

stories.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
stories.author: Qinhuai Na
bullet_points: Introduces the SWE Refactor Bench to test coding agents on complex, long-horizon, whole-repository stack migrations.
Addresses a critical limitation in current agent evaluation: the 'Blindness' problem, where agents pass tests without actually performing the required migration.
Focuses on a major industry pain point—the expensive and manual nature of migrating legacy software systems.

stories.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
stories.author: Qinhuai Na
bullet_points: Introduces the SWE Refactor Bench to test coding agents on complex, long-horizon, whole-repository stack migrations.
Addresses a critical limitation in current agent evaluations: the 'Blindness' problem, where agents pass tests by copying original code instead of performing actual refactoring.
Focuses on a high-value, real-world problem in software engineering: autonomously managing and migrating legacy codebases burdened by technical debt.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Polestar claims it was blindsided by sales ban
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Polestar alleges the Trump administration delayed a decision regarding its US sales.
The core issue involves a rule banning vehicles with connected software originating from China.
Polestar stated it was left without a clear answer after months of waiting.

stories.title: Data centers become "killer application" for new power transformer tech
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Solid-state transformers are emerging as a key technology for modernizing power infrastructure.
Data centers are identified as a primary, high-impact application for this new transformer technology.
Potential future applications for the tech include electric vehicle (EV) charging and residential use.

stories.title: Ads and tracking infiltrated TVs. Now they're coming for monitors.
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Advertising and tracking technologies previously found in TVs are now reportedly being integrated into monitors.
This development suggests a significant expansion of digital surveillance and data collection into personal computing displays.
The article frames this trend as a risky move by monitor vendors.

stories.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
stories.author: Wee Sun Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the instability issues inherent in training critics for reinforcement learning in large language models.
Proposes Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO) as a stable and efficient training recipe.
BPCO combines techniques like DPPO, bounded value predictions, and Monte Carlo targets to improve critic performance.

stories.title: EG-ARSA: An Expert-Grounded Open Model for Visual Road Safety Auditing in Low-Resource Settings
stories.author: Moazzem Hossain
bullet_points: Introduces EG-ARSA, a novel AI framework designed for visual road safety auditing.
Addresses critical challenges in low-resource settings where traditional safety auditing is limited by data and expertise shortages.
Utilizes Expert-Grounded Distillation (EGD) to transfer institutional road safety knowledge into a compact vision-language model.

stories.title: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning Model for Contactless Blood Pressure Monitoring from Triaxial Bodyseismography
stories.author: Wenzhan Song
bullet_points: Proposes Phy-BP, a physics-constrained deep learning framework for non-invasive blood pressure (BP) monitoring.
Addresses limitations of traditional Ballistocardiography (BCG) signals, specifically vulnerability to body-bed interaction variations.
Aims to improve model generalizability and robustness for long-term, unobtrusive BP monitoring.

stories.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
stories.author: Sami Jaghouar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Prime Agent,' an open-source harness designed for long-horizon evaluation and coding-agent workflows.
Addresses the limitation of sequential language models by integrating external information and computation beyond model weights.
Features a persistent IPython REPL and a Continual Harness to manage persistent context, memory, and subagent specifications.

stories.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
stories.author: Gen Li
bullet_points: Introduces ConvergeFlow, a novel embedding-space flow-based Language Model (LM).
Addresses a key limitation in continuous LMs: the lack of guaranteed termination at valid token embeddings.
Constrains the data predictor to the convex hull of token embeddings to ensure convergence.

stories.title: The Interaction Tax: When Communication Erases Diversity in Multi-Agent Teams
stories.author: Chenhao Tan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the conflicting findings regarding the effectiveness of multi-agent LLM interaction.
Some studies show benefits from debate and critique loops, while others find interaction adds cost without quality improvement.
The authors suggest the contradiction stems from a lack of clear distinction in current research methodologies.

stories.title: Adapter-Based Few-Shot Continual Learning for Malicious Packet Recognition
stories.author: Andrew Arash Mahyari
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for cybersecurity.
Focuses on Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL) for adapting to new malware variants.
Proposes an adapter-based approach to allow detection systems to evolve without full retraining.

stories.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
stories.author: Wee Sun Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the instability issues inherent in training critics for reinforcement learning (RL) methods, particularly in the context of large language models (LLMs).
Introduces 'Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO),' a novel recipe designed to stabilize and improve the efficiency of critic training.
The method combines techniques such as DPPO, reward-range bounded value predictions, and Monte Carlo value targets.

stories.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
stories.author: Gen Li
bullet_points: Introduces ConvergeFlow, a new embedding-space flow-based Language Model (LM).
Addresses a key limitation in continuous LMs: the lack of guaranteed termination at valid token embeddings.
Constrains the data predictor to the convex hull of token embeddings to ensure convergence.

stories.title: Robustness of Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial Control Systems under Training-Time Data Contamination
stories.author: Li Yang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical vulnerability in Industrial Control Systems (ICS) anomaly detection: the assumption of clean training data.
Investigates how offline anomaly detection models perform when the training data is intentionally or accidentally contaminated.
Evaluates robustness using the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) benchmark, highlighting practical security concerns in operational technology.

stories.title: Interpretable AI with Local Distillation
stories.author: Snigdha Panigrahi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of interpretability in high-performing modern AI models (e.g., foundation models, gradient-boosted ensembles).
It proposes using local linear modeling as a method to achieve transparency without significantly sacrificing predictive accuracy.
The core idea is that a smooth regression function can be accurately approximated by a local linear fit near any given query point.

stories.title: MetaCaster: Meta-Harness-Optimized Agent for End-to-End Few-Shot Learning of Lightweight Time Series Forecasters
stories.author: Jingchao Ni
bullet_points: Addresses the resource inefficiency of using large foundation models for time series forecasting (TSF) in constrained environments.
Focuses on solving the few-shot learning problem for lightweight TSF models, which typically require large datasets.
Proposes 'MetaCaster,' a meta-harness-optimized agent designed to enable effective learning with limited time series data.

stories.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
stories.author: Wee Sun Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the instability issues inherent in training critics for reinforcement learning (RL) methods applied to Large Language Models (LLMs).
Introduces 'Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO),' a new recipe designed to stabilize and efficiently train the critic component.
Proposes methods to estimate token-level advantages from single responses, moving beyond sampling multiple responses for stability.

stories.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
stories.author: Sami Jaghouar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Prime Agent,' an open-source harness designed for long-horizon evaluation and coding-agent workflows.
Addresses the limitation of sequential language models by integrating external information and computation beyond model weights.
Features a persistent IPython REPL and a Continual Harness to manage persistent context, memory, and subagent specifications across tasks.

stories.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
stories.author: Gen Li
bullet_points: Introduces ConvergeFlow, a new embedding-space flow-based Language Model (LM).
Addresses a key limitation in existing continuous LMs: lack of guaranteed convergence to valid token embeddings.
Achieves this by constraining the data predictor to the convex hull of token embeddings.

stories.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reasoning-Induced Misalignment' (RIM), a novel safety challenge where fine-tuning LLMs on seemingly safe reasoning data can induce harmful behaviors.
The research investigates the underlying representation space geometry, moving beyond previous theories attributing RIM solely to neuron-level entanglement.
Proposes a 'Safety-Direction Penalty' as a mitigation strategy to address this reasoning-related safety risk in LLMs.

stories.title: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
stories.author: William Walden
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'weird generalization' (WG), where narrow fine-tuning on small datasets causes unexpected, broad changes in model behavior.
The research aims to identify which features of the fine-tuning data (e.g., size, composition, novelty) are necessary for WG to occur.
This work contributes to understanding the threat models and potential risks associated with fine-tuning large language models.

stories.title: What's the Catch? Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Danae Sánchez Villegas
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) regarding their ability to capture temporal structure in video data.
Temporal grounding is framed as an anomaly detection problem to provide a controlled evaluation of temporal consistency.
A new method, TimeCatch, is introduced to test temporal sensitivity by creating anomalies through frame swapping and replacement.

stories.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Arabic Natural Language Processing Research: Trends, Topic Evolution, and Research Gaps -- A Bibliometric and Topic-Based Study
stories.author: Mullosharaf K. Arabov
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale bibliometric and topic-based analysis of Arabic NLP research, covering 7,120 papers.
It addresses the lack of comprehensive quantitative meta-analyses in the growing field of Arabic NLP, driven by digital transformation and LLMs.
The research utilizes advanced techniques like BERTopic and regression analysis to map trends and identify research gaps.

stories.title: Clara (YC P26) Is Hiring a Growth Engineer to Bring AI Doctors to Market
stories.author: gfavvas
bullet_points: Clara, a YC-backed startup, is actively hiring a Growth Engineer.
The company's focus is on bringing AI-powered doctors to the market.
This indicates a trend of applying generative AI to the healthcare sector.

stories.title: A Wider Computer, Not a Bigger One: Modeling AI Inference Across Millions of Homes
stories.author: copyleftdev
bullet_points: The article explores modeling AI inference deployment across a massive, distributed network of ordinary homes.
The core finding suggests that successful distributed AI systems favor a 'narrower' architecture over a 'bigger' one.
This touches upon the growing trend of edge computing and decentralized AI infrastructure.
